result.title: Designing Informative Actions: Action Construction for Long-Horizon Research Agents
result.summary: Large language model agents support automated scientific research by connecting literature analysis and planning with experimentation. Evaluating which action an agent selects does not establish which experiment its instruction specifies, because omitted interventions or replication counts leave consequential choices to the executor. We introduce a reading-set framework for evaluating action construction under a common cost rule. Across 30 synthetic states, complete-design requests increase affordable efficiency by 465.98% and 327.91% relative to the action-name baseline in the two model families, respectively. An author-constructed research-action evaluation dataset provides 60 scenarios for complementary judgment evaluation. On this dataset, the scenario-level information-per-cost measure has a mean within-scenario correlation of 0.733 with judgments from 18 human participants. The framework makes design specification and execution ambiguity measurable, providing a reproducible basis for assessing how research agents translate scientific intent into informative, budget-feasible experiments.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 reading-set 框架，在统一成本规则下评估研究智能体的动作构造，即指令所指定的实验设计是否完整；在 30 个合成状态上比较不同动作表述的可负担效率，并用 60 个场景数据集检验 scenario 级 information-per-cost 与人类判断的相关性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「信息量除以成本」度量与「动作指令歧义可测量」的思路，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK 类证据获取动作的收益—成本评价与动作规格设计提供概念借鉴，但属跨领域启发，是否适用于视觉证据筛选尚待核查。
